title: Monochrome Enamel Hoops
category: Earrings (chunky enamel C hoop with a post, sold as 1 pair)
metal: 18k gold tone (tag '18k Gold Tone Plated'; the description says only 'Finish: Gold tone' and names no plating or base metal). Mirror-polished, warm yellow, not orange: earlier measurement on the rails gave Lab 66-71 / 10-14 / 27-37, hue 63-75 degrees. Glossy opaque black and white enamel.
lock: 1 pair of chunky open-C post hoops, 20 mm tall, 7 mm wide, mirror-polished 18k gold tone. Each front: 2 glossy enamel stripes side by side, 1 black, 1 white, near-equal width, between 3 gold-tone rails (2 rounded edges, 1 fine centre). Inside plain polished 18k gold tone, softly ribbed, no enamel. 1 thin post at the top end, 0 stones. Must stay exactly 1 black + 1 white stripe on an open C, never more or alternating bands, never a closed ring.
morph: The stripes. Image models multiply the 1 + 1 enamel stripes into alternating black-white bands (zebra or piano-key rows), swap the enamel for onyx, pearl or stones, turn the white cream, or drop the fine centre rail so the two colours touch. Second risk: the open C closes into a full ring or turns into a hinged huggie. Third: scale. In ads-500 b03-4 the model ignored a size clause and drew the pair larger on the retry (19.9-21.4 px/mm against 14-17 allowed). At the three-quarter pose, height / width is 1.37 on the pack ref, not the 1.65 an old brief used.
sizeMm: Approximately 20 mm tall and 7 mm wide, give or take 1 mm (listing description and the size-guide photo 05). My cross-check on worn photo 04: one hoop hangs from the lobe at about a third of the ear's height, about 20-21 mm if the ear is 60 mm tall, which agrees. Referents: as tall as a 2019-series Rs 1 coin is wide (20 mm). The 7 mm band is about as thick as a pencil.

variants: 1 variant: Default Title (SKU MEH), 18k gold tone, stock 24 (compare-at Rs 1,249; never print the struck price). Every photo shows this one tone, and there is no rhodium silver tone option. Show the pair (02), or one hoop as a macro (01). At 24 it sits 4 units above the 20-unit floor, so it is never an anchor or card 5.
story: The only black-and-white piece in the range, and the most graphic thing in it. Three colours that already go with everything (black, white, gold tone) are compressed into a 20 mm hoop that is still legible as a thumbnail. The b04-0 float ad, a card-only zero-credit frame, came out of the blind re-test at 7.74, beating both winners and both losers with both critics. It is chunky enough (7 mm) to read from across a room, yet small enough for office days. Lovable details: the fine gold-tone centre rail that separates night from day like piping on a tuxedo lapel, and the plain ribbed gold inside, which reads as a secret when the hoop turns. Rhymes, each on 1 black + 1 white, never a row: a black and a white chess piece side by side; kajal eyes with a white chikankari kurta; one black and one white piano key; a black Bakelite switch on a white wall; ink on paper (a fountain-pen nib, a newspaper fold); a Bombay Art Deco black-and-white floor; a 1960s black-and-white film still, shown in colour only through the gold tone; the pair as round brackets ( ); a panda or a magpie as a theatrical joke. Colour tension also works: the listing's own worn shot sets it on marigold satin, and the plan sets it against haldi yellow and deep teal. Styling from the listing: a crisp white shirt, or all in black.
copyNotes: Use: gold tone (preferred in body copy), 18k gold tone (allowed on the tag's authority), enamel, glossy enamel, black and white, monochrome, C hoop, chunky, post back, about 20 mm, 7 mm wide, one pair, 'one black, one white', crisp white shirt / all in black. Avoid: gold or silver alone as the metal, real or solid gold, '18k gold' without 'tone'; PVD, surgical stainless steel, steel, brass or any base metal (not stated); waterproof, tarnish free, anti-tarnish, hypoallergenic, sweat-proof, shower, gym, swim, and any durability promise for the enamel (no 'won't chip'); any water imagery (rain, pool, drops, wet or glossy-wet grounds), because the care text says keep it dry; stone or material words: onyx, ceramic, pearl, mother-of-pearl, cubic zirconia, crystal, diamond; huggie, hinged, clicker, sleeper; 'stripes' as a pattern, zebra print, candy stripe, or anything that implies more than 2 bands; brand names for the black-white-gold couture look. Never quote the compare-at price.

photos.shows: Detail: one hoop standing on cream, three-quarter view. The black stripe is on the left and the white on the right, between 3 polished rails (the left edge rail thin, a fine centre rail, the right edge rail rounded and fuller as it turns toward the inside). The open C shows the inside: plain polished gold tone with 3 soft rounded ribs, no enamel. A thin straight post rises from the top end and points back. 18k gold tone. Same photo as the size guide. Reference 2 (media id 2ee2cf91).

Packshot: the pair standing side by side on a cream plaster cube against a cream sweep. The two hoops are identical, not mirrored: black left, white right, post upper right, open side right. 18k gold tone. Clearest view of the whole construction as a pair. Reference 1 (media id 970635a3).

Worn, three-quarter profile: dark straight hair, a marigold satin cami, fingers at the collarbone, the lower face cropped. The hoop sits on the lobe with the white stripe toward the cheek; small in frame, it reads as an everyday size. 18k gold tone.

Worn close-up: the ear and lobe, with the hoop hanging at about a third of the ear's height (about 20-21 mm estimated). The stripes face forward, white toward the face and black behind, with a gold rail at each edge and one between. Marigold strap. True scale, so it is the best worn scale photo. 18k gold tone.

Size guide: photo 01 with a 20 mm height bar, and the text '20 mm tall · 7 mm wide · give or take 1 mm' plus the NAIRA PETITE wordmark. Scale evidence only; it has a text overlay, so it is not a generation reference.
